topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening introduces the lecturer and situates the session within the cancer course while setting out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer-causing mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations arise and enable clonal evolution within a biological environment that permits cancer development.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of intrinsic bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental mutagens produce DNA damage and mutations through mechanisms shaped by their chemical properties and biological processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from promotion by showing how a permissive environment enables initiated cells to form tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological context determines susceptibility to carcinogens and conclude by relating that specificity to the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be detected and attributed to exposures, emphasizing the evidential strengths and limitations of the available methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions and frames their practical implications as everyday risk–benefit decisions.
